builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
summary: The method replaces a conventionally deeper transformer with a shallower one whose weights are applied repeatedly, optionally with small per-loop low-rank adapters, to increase effective depth without increasing parameter count. The cost is a decoding slowdown proportional to the number of loops, plus training from scratch at up to 1B parameters and 155B tokens to realize the reported gains. Gains can saturate, reverse, or become unstable with more loops, and the parallel formulation does not reliably preserve quality without specific normalization changes.
rationale: The technique requires training models from scratch at a scale beyond the reader's constrained infrastructure, so it is relevant to track but not practical to adopt now.

claims.statement: The method replaces a conventionally deeper transformer with a shallower one whose weights are applied repeatedly, optionally with small per-loop low-rank adapters, to increase effective depth without increasing parameter count. The cost is a decoding slowdown proportional to the number of loops, plus training from scratch at up to 1B parameters and 155B tokens to realize the reported gains. Gains can saturate, reverse, or become unstable with more loops, and the parallel formulation does not reliably preserve quality without specific normalization changes.
Looping the full transformer gives the strongest quality at a fixed parameter budget; small loop-specific low-rank adapters improve quality, with larger gains as more loops are added.
